plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $36, bidding exactly $36 ensures I only win when profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay. This is optimal for maximizing expected profit in this one-shot second-price auction.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying only that second-highest bid, and never overpay. Bidding above value risks winning at a price above your value (loss), while bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single-round game with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my value of $32 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own), there's no incentive to shade the bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and this being the only round, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my private value of $42 to maximize expected profit.
